objective:
Capture the agreed Mythos V2/V3 architecture so it is not forgotten.

minimize Claude token usage while maximizing reuse.
scope: This issue is a durable architecture/roadmap record. It does not authorize implementation by itself. The V2 master execution plan should be created from this and the current codebase before autonomous V2 execution begins.

[core v2 principle]
Before Qwen starts a substantial task, FABLE should determine whether existing strong/open-source projects, libraries, runtimes, skills, or models can be reused.

Flow:

FABLE → determine whether research is needed → Sonnet/Opus research → evaluate candidates → FABLE makes the execution decision → REUSE / ADAPT / CONNECT / BUILD LAST → Qwen executes → mechanical validation/review.

[research policy]
Research is not a generic “best project” ranking. It must evaluate concrete candidates against the task requirements, including where relevant:

- repository/project
- license
- maintenance/activity
- architecture
- dependencies
- compatibility with Mythos/Haddad
- security implications
- expected reuse percentage
- required adaptations
- integration cost
- risks
- whether it can run on current hardware
- whether it is genuinely free/open-weight/open-source where applicable

FABLE remains the execution authority. Sonnet/Opus are research/architecture advisors, not the final authority and not the default executor.

[model escalation]
- Simple task / no meaningful reuse question → Qwen directly.
- Reuse/integration research → Sonnet research when sufficient.
- Architecture/security/complex integration → Opus research.
- Ambiguous/high-impact research decision → Opus arbitration.
- Qwen remains the local executor.

[v2 phases]
1. V2.1 — AI Team Foundation
2. V2.2 — FABLE Task Delegation
3. V2.3 — Parallel Workers + Resource Awareness
4. V2.4 — OTHKM Integration
5. V2.5 — AI Team Console
6. V2.6 — Autonomous Continuous Operation

Each phase advances only after capability + tests + evidence + safety + real E2E gates pass. No time-based promotion.

[qwen capability ladder]
The V2 master plan must define what Qwen must demonstrably be able to do at each phase before promotion. Do not accept “Qwen says it succeeded”; use mechanical validation, evidence, scope checks, tests, review and delivery.

[jev — future, not v2 dependency]
Later, introduce Jev as a decision/router layer that can choose the most appropriate research strategy and possibly which researcher/model/tools to invoke.

Future flow:

FABLE → Jev → choose research strategy → Sonnet/Opus research → FABLE decision → Qwen execution.

Jev must not become the executor and must not be a V2 prerequisite.

[future model discovery]
Later Jev + Sonnet/Opus can help discover free/open models suitable for Haddad/model library.

Candidate evaluation should include:

- truly free vs paid API
- open weights/source status
- license
- VRAM/RAM requirements
- inference speed
- CUDA/Vulkan/CPU compatibility
- context length
- coding/reasoning quality
- GGUF/llama.cpp availability
- quantized variants
- commercial-use constraints
- maintenance/activity
- benchmark on Haddad before acceptance

Future model onboarding:

DISCOVER → VERIFY → BENCHMARK → SECURITY REVIEW → ACCEPT/REJECT.

Do not install many models merely because they are popular.

[parallel work]
Haddad Live Console in status.mythosprod.xyz continues in parallel and should reuse VPS MCP + Haddad MCP and existing monitoring/health/event infrastructure.

[reuse rule]
SEARCH → REUSE → ADAPT → CONNECT → BUILD LAST.

Do not build duplicate scheduler, executor, provider, validation, retry, MCP, memory, monitoring stack, or other infrastructure when an existing Mythos component can be reused.
